newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hopewell interim operating profit soars.
newsitem.headline: Hopewell interim operating profit soars.

text.p: Hopewell Holdings Ltd said on Friday its operating profit jumped 89 percent to HK$769 million for the half-year ended December 31, 1996, while net profit rose 7.7 percent to HK$502 million.
Earnings per share were 11.5 Hong Kong cents against 10.7 cents a year earlier, the company said in a statement.

"Without taking into account of the writeback of tax provision for the six months ended 31st December 1995, the earnings per share for that (comparative) period would be 6.2 cents," the infrastructure firm said.
Hopewell said it signed a preliminary agreement last November with Chinese partners to improve and operate a 40.7-km toll road in Shunde city, Guangdong province.
The road, with an estimated project cost of 1.5 billion yuan, will connect Nanhai and Zhongshan in the Pearl River Delta region, it said.
In Bangkok, construction had started on the east route, from Samsen to Huamak, of its Bangkok Elevated Road and Train System (BERTS) while work continued on the north line, Hopewell said.
"Progress is on track to allow opening of the tollway by the time of the Asian Games in Bangkok in December 1998," it added.
